caption: Fig 2: Level 1 of Terra-Audit. The root use case decomposes into seven first-level capability areas — Field Management, Satellite Data Engine, MRV Signal Analytics, Carbon Estimation, Evidence Reporting, AI Validation, and Cropland ALM Practice & Credit Entry — each expanded further below.
title: Level 1 of Terra-Audit. The root use case decomposes into seven first-level capability areas — Field Management, Satellite Data Engine, MRV Signal Analytics, Carbon Estimation, Evidence Reporting, AI Validation, and Cropland ALM Practice & Credit Entry — each expanded further below.

caption: Fig 3: Field Management (Use Case 1.1). The developer registers, selects, and deletes fields; this level decomposes into Geometry Input (1.1.1) and Field Registration (1.1.2).
title: Field Management (Use Case 1.1). The developer registers, selects, and deletes fields; this level decomposes into Geometry Input (1.1.1) and Field Registration (1.1.2).

caption: Fig 4: Geometry Input (Use Case 1.1.1). The developer supplies a field boundary by drawing on the map, uploading a GeoJSON/KML file, or pasting GPS coordinates; malformed input returns a readable error instead of crashing the app.
title: Geometry Input (Use Case 1.1.1). The developer supplies a field boundary by drawing on the map, uploading a GeoJSON/KML file, or pasting GPS coordinates; malformed input returns a readable error instead of crashing the app.

caption: Fig 5: Field Registration (Use Case 1.1.2). Once a geometry is validated, the system computes area via the Shoelace formula with spherical correction and persists the field — ID, name, district, geometry, area, and field type — to the SQLite registry.
title: Field Registration (Use Case 1.1.2). Once a geometry is validated, the system computes area via the Shoelace formula with spherical correction and persists the field — ID, name, district, geometry, area, and field type — to the SQLite registry.

caption: Fig 6: Satellite Data Engine (Use Case 1.2). For rice_awd fields, retrieves Sentinel-1 VV/VH backscatter over the field geometry (DESCENDING pass only) from Google Earth Engine, checking the local cache first and persisting any newly fetched observations for instant reuse.
title: Satellite Data Engine (Use Case 1.2). For rice_awd fields, retrieves Sentinel-1 VV/VH backscatter over the field geometry (DESCENDING pass only) from Google Earth Engine, checking the local cache first and persisting any newly fetched observations for instant reuse.

caption: Fig 7: MRV Signal Analytics (Use Case 1.3). Applies Savitzky-Golay smoothing, z-score flood detection, drydown-event detection, and VH-based phenology extraction to the cached time-series; the researcher may substitute an AI-assisted detector for the rule-based gate.
title: MRV Signal Analytics (Use Case 1.3). Applies Savitzky-Golay smoothing, z-score flood detection, drydown-event detection, and VH-based phenology extraction to the cached time-series; the researcher may substitute an AI-assisted detector for the rule-based gate.

caption: Fig 8: Carbon Estimation (Use Case 1.4). Computes VM0051 QA3 rice credits or VM0042 cropland ALM credits depending on the field’s type, exposing every intermediate value in the ledger for hand verification.
title: Carbon Estimation (Use Case 1.4). Computes VM0051 QA3 rice credits or VM0042 cropland ALM credits depending on the field’s type, exposing every intermediate value in the ledger for hand verification.

caption: Fig 9: Evidence Reporting (Use Case 1.5). Packages the field record, monitoring window, satellite or practice data, and carbon calculation into a downloadable PDF report, JSON audit record, and CSV.
title: Evidence Reporting (Use Case 1.5). Packages the field record, monitoring window, satellite or practice data, and carbon calculation into a downloadable PDF report, JSON audit record, and CSV.

caption: Fig 10: AI Validation (Use Case 1.6). The researcher builds a labeled dataset, trains Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers, and compares their agreement with the rule-based gate via precision/recall/F1, confusion matrices, feature importance, and ROC curves.
title: AI Validation (Use Case 1.6). The researcher builds a labeled dataset, trains Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers, and compares their agreement with the rule-based gate via precision/recall/F1, confusion matrices, feature importance, and ROC curves.

caption: Fig 11: Cropland ALM Practice & Credit Entry (Use Case 1.7). The developer enters the practice schedule, livestock schedule, and crop yield; runs the production-decline leakage screen; calculates VM0042 credits; and can separately view calculation history or edit the field's name/district.
title: Cropland ALM Practice & Credit Entry (Use Case 1.7). The developer enters the practice schedule, livestock schedule, and crop yield; runs the production-decline leakage screen; calculates VM0042 credits; and can separately view calculation history or edit the field's name/district.

caption: Fig 12: Terra-Audit (Activity — Use Case 1). The top-level flow: a field is registered, analytics are run, credits are calculated according to the field’s methodology path, and evidence is exported.
title: Terra-Audit (Activity — Use Case 1). The top-level flow: a field is registered, analytics are run, credits are calculated according to the field’s methodology path, and evidence is exported.

caption: Fig 13: Field Management (Activity — Use Case 1.1). Draw, upload, or paste a boundary; validate; compute area; persist the field record.
title: Field Management (Activity — Use Case 1.1). Draw, upload, or paste a boundary; validate; compute area; persist the field record.

caption: Fig 14: Geometry Input & Registration (Activity — Use Case 1.1.1). The three input methods converge on a single validation and registration path, so any input source produces an identical stored field record.
title: Geometry Input & Registration (Activity — Use Case 1.1.1). The three input methods converge on a single validation and registration path, so any input source produces an identical stored field record.

caption: Fig 15: Satellite Data Engine (Activity — Use Case 1.2). Check the cache; on a miss, query Earth Engine, compute derived indices, smooth the signal, and write the result back to the cache.
title: Satellite Data Engine (Activity — Use Case 1.2). Check the cache; on a miss, query Earth Engine, compute derived indices, smooth the signal, and write the result back to the cache.

caption: Fig 16: MRV Signal Analytics (Activity — Use Case 1.3). Standardize VV into z-scores, flag flooded states, detect drydown events, extract phenology, and — if an AI model is selected and trained — overwrite the rule-based flags with model predictions plus a confidence score.
title: MRV Signal Analytics (Activity — Use Case 1.3). Standardize VV into z-scores, flag flooded states, detect drydown events, extract phenology, and — if an AI model is selected and trained — overwrite the rule-based flags with model predictions plus a confidence score.

caption: Fig 17: Carbon Estimation (Activity — Use Case 1.4). Branches on field type: the VM0051 QA3 steps (water scaling, uncertainty deduction, N₂O penalty) for rice fields, or the extended VM0042 steps (SOC stock change, livestock emissions, leakage screen, uncertainty and buffer deduction) for cropland fields; both paths floor final issuance at zero and persist the result to credit history.
title: Carbon Estimation (Activity — Use Case 1.4). Branches on field type: the VM0051 QA3 steps (water scaling, uncertainty deduction, N₂O penalty) for rice fields, or the extended VM0042 steps (SOC stock change, livestock emissions, leakage screen, uncertainty and buffer deduction) for cropland fields; both paths floor final issuance at zero and persist the result to credit history.

caption: Fig 18: Evidence Reporting (Activity — Use Case 1.5). Assemble the field, window, signal/practice, and carbon data into the PDF and JSON generators (and the CSV generator for practice/SOC data), then serve each as a browser download.
title: Evidence Reporting (Activity — Use Case 1.5). Assemble the field, window, signal/practice, and carbon data into the PDF and JSON generators (and the CSV generator for practice/SOC data), then serve each as a browser download.

caption: Fig 19: AI Validation (Activity — Use Case 1.6). Build the labeled dataset, engineer leakage-safe features, train both classifiers with cross-validation, then evaluate and compare them.
title: AI Validation (Activity — Use Case 1.6). Build the labeled dataset, engineer leakage-safe features, train both classifiers with cross-validation, then evaluate and compare them.
